newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares slip on enlarged volume.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares slip on enlarged volume.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down on Tuesday on enlarged volume with overseas institutions dumping stocks with poor results later in the session, brokers said.
The index ended down 0.388 points or 0.79 percent to 48.696 points on volume of 9.4 million shares worth $3.0 million. Of 41 B shares, 35 traded with 12 down, 19 flat and four up.
"After five days' of rises on speculative buying, heavy selling emerged again in the late session, which caused the market to slip," one broker said.

"Recently, trading volume has been thin while prices have been rising, but trading volume grew with today's fall. This means the market will move down further in the coming days with bearish market sentiment reigning," he added.
The textile sector led today's falling list with investors concerned about the possible effects of U.S. controls on China's textiles quotas.

China Textile was the biggest loser, plunging $0.020 or 18.18 percent to $0.090 on volume of 102,500 shares. Shanghai Erfangji Textile followed, tumbling $0.012 or 11.76 percent to $0.090 on volume of 69,900 shares.
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation traded the most on institutional cross-trading, ending unchanged at $0.132 on volume of 1.5 million shares.
Shanghai A shares rallied in active trading on good market sentiment, brokers said.

The index gained 14.092 points or 1.55 percent to 921.272 points on volume of 511.6 million shares worth 4.3 billion yuan. The SSE blue-chip index ended up 42.728 points or 1.79 percent to 2429.058 points.
Zhengzhou Baiwen was the star on speculative buying, surging 0.79 yuan or 12.17 percent to 7.28 yuan on volume of 18.5 million shares.
